_readme: The 9-slide webinar storyline Alex describes at 46:59-48:09 in the 2026-09-04 sales training. He was pointing at a list on his screen ('it's like 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9') and narrated each step aloud. These are the STEPS - the job each slide does - not the headlines. Headlines are written per prospect from the brief.
_lineage: Fireflies transcript -> the brief (extracted_data) -> these slides. Every slide declares the brief field it reads from in 'source'. Where source is null the brief has no field for it yet and the copy here is INFERRED - Geri's transcript-to-brief step needs to start emitting those four.
_style: Sparse. Alex: 'probably you give them one sentence to it', 'just one sentence, like really'. The whole storyline is 'two, three minutes' across nine slides - about fifteen seconds each. A headline and one line. Never a paragraph.
_case_study_warning: Slide 6 is the PROSPECT'S case study - one of THEIR clients, shown to THEIR audience. It is NOT a Quantum Scaling client. The QS case-study library (Airtable) is used on the Lead List and Calendar Invite, where we are proving OUR results to the prospect. Different direction. Do not wire Airtable into this slide.

slides.headline: Your margin isn't leaking in the machines. It's leaking in the handoffs.
slides.line: A 90-minute working session for industrial operators carrying cost they can't see.

slides.headline: Built for one room, not a general audience.
slides.line: COOs and VP Operations at 50-500 person industrial and manufacturing firms across North America and Western Europe.

slides.headline: Referrals stopped scaling, and nothing replaced them.
slides.line: Growth is entirely referral-driven and has flattened - with no repeatable way to reach new operators.

slides.headline: On your own most conservative numbers, this is what a year of waiting costs.
slides.line: Three retainers a month not won, at a $32,000 deal size, is $1.1M of contracted revenue that never enters the pipeline. Deliberately the low estimate — the real figure is larger.
slides.inferred_from: Alex 47:15 'you make the problem big and demonstrate the impact of not changing — just one sentence'. The NUMBER follows his conservative-inputs rule at 48:41: 'you always calculate with the lowest possible inputs you can find… I even downgraded by another 5%. I really want to go as low as somehow possible.' Stating the loss at the low end is what makes it unarguable. Math: extracted_data.goals (3 retainers/mo) x business.deal_size ($32,000).

slides.headline: Three new retainers a month. No new delivery hires.
slides.line: Operating cost per unit down 18-30% within two quarters.

slides.headline: A 200-person plastics manufacturer in Ohio.
slides.before: Changeover eating a full shift; margin invisible below the line item.
slides.note: The PROSPECT'S client, not ours. Dummy data in the prototype - in production this comes from the prospect's own case study in the brief.

slides.headline: Start from the three clients a month. Work backwards.
slides.line: We don't start from what we can send. We start from the result you want, then reverse-engineer the invite volume that gets you there — calibrated to what your delivery team can actually absorb.
slides.inferred_from: Alex 51:39-51:57 verbatim: 'I always say we invite 1.2 million… but your results, what you actually want to achieve is three clients per month. Now let's back engineer that. That's a reverse engineer process.' Plus Ryan 52:23: 'we're going to calibrate this to what you can actually handle, your capacity.' This slide is a REVERSE-ENGINEER, not a calendar timeline — the earlier draft had that wrong.

slides.headline: Four risks, moved off your side of the table.

risks.answer: Modelled on your lowest numbers, not your best month. If it only works at the optimistic end, we say so.
Diagnosis before build. We size the market first — if it isn't there, you don't proceed.
One operator owns your account end to end. No handoff to a delivery team you've never met.
Your team stays on delivery. Roughly an hour a week from you, once it's running.

slides.inferred_from: Alex names the four risks verbatim at 47:54: 'the investment risk, the failure risk, the communication gap risk, the time investment risk'. The ANSWERS are inferred, and deliberately structural rather than guarantee-based, because Alex at 35:11: 'you only use guarantees if you really need it.'

slides.step: The offer, and three ways in
slides.headline: Three ways in. Each one leaves you with something.
slides.line: Whether or not you go further.

ctas.cta: A deep analysis of your situation
ctas.detail: We size your addressable market and show you the arithmetic. You keep it.
The system running on your numbers and your market, not a generic walkthrough.

ctas.cta: [ third CTA not specified in the call ]
ctas.detail: Alex named two of the three. This slot needs his input.

slides.inferred_from: Alex 47:59: 'you go into your solution offering and you give three key CTAs that are high value with a deep analysis of their situation and create a custom demo.' Only TWO of the three are named in the transcript. The third is left explicitly blank rather than invented — Alex has to fill it.

_inferred_note: Slides 4, 7, 8 and 9 have no brief field yet. Their copy is inferred from the 2026-09-04 sales-training transcript, where Alex teaches his method for each. Every one records its derivation and timestamp in 'inferred_from' so it can be checked against the tape. Slide 9's third CTA is left BLANK on purpose: Alex named only two.
